dev.reply:
Yes
Clear, workable, and directly protects developer flow. Swallowed push refusals and unverified commits waste substantial time during card development, especially when working through tight red/green test cycles and slice limits. Verifying the exit code unpiped, confirming remote head via fetch, and checking commits with git log -1 prevents phantom progress and stale branch states without adding unreasonable friction. The 3-card trial with explicit metrics makes it low-risk and fair to the work.
CITE: every push writes its whole output and its own exit code to a file
